title: Find a Word in a Text
statement:
Find the index where a word first appears inside a text.

The first line is the text, made of lowercase letters and single spaces. The second line is the word, made of lowercase letters with no spaces. Print the index where the first copy of the word starts in the text, counting from 0, where every space counts as a character too. Print `-1` when the word does not appear. Your language can do this search in one call, but here you write the matching yourself, so leave that call out.

Input:

```text
the cat sat on the mat
sat
```

Expected output:

```text
8
```

tests.stdin:
the cat sat on the mat
sat

hints: Try every position in the text as a start. At each one, compare the word's characters with the text's characters from that position on, one pair at a time, and give up on that start at the first pair that differs.
The word only fits where enough of the text is left for all of it. When the word is longer than the text, there is no start to try at all.

Outside this exercise, you would call the built-in search: `text.find(word)` in Python, `text.indexOf(word)` in JavaScript and Java, `text.find(word)` in C++ (which gives `std::string::npos` when the word is missing), and `strings.Index(text, word)` in Go.
